title: Fall of Nineveh to Babylon and the Medes
summary: Fall of Nineveh to Babylon and the Medes
description: Record first created by the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). CFAH dates it as well (added by the CFAH pass); the sort follows the four-tier rule.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 1: CFAH anchor point: 612 BC (AP-84, OSF preprint CFAH-14). Sort changed by the CFAH pass (2026-10-18): was provisional (Generations) 612 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "CFAH-14: Ancient Assyria," OSF preprint v1.0 (27 Feb 2026), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/9FUW2, file CFAH-14_Assyria_v_1.0.pdf, p. 16, heading "Fall of Nineveh - 612 BC -Anchor Point #84"
Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 11 "Babylon Has Fallen (626–539 BC)", PDF p. 330 (printed p. 329)
chronologies.note: Nabopolassar with the Medes takes Nippur and Ashur (615 BC) and Nineveh; also pp. 321, 364.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "612 BC" (PDF p. 481): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 19 "Babylon Has Fallen", PDF p. 481 (printed p. 467)
Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 42 (PDF p. 50)
chronologies.note: From the book's "Ancient Empires" pages (credited in an image to Daily Bible Study, keyway.ca). The reign of Sin-shar-ishkun ends with the fall of Nineveh.

chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.106 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 49 (PDF p. 51)
chronologies.note: After the Scythian period the Medes under Cyaxares recover their empire and take Nineveh. Generations dates the fall of Nineveh to 612 BC (provisional). That is inside the CFAH-derived reign of Cyaxares (635/634–595/594 BC), so consistent.

free_source_links.locator: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)
